description: T3a whole-file prefilter for curating KB v6 (docs/rule_change_v6_plan.md T3a). drop = no content on the form of the four exercises usable for any of the 12 rules; unsure = keep. pending = not assessed, waiting for the user. entries.path: data/bicep-curl/Exertional Rhabdomyolysis in a 21-year-old, Healthy Female after Performing Three Sets of the Biceps Curl Exercise to Failure with 30% 1rm A Case Report.pdf
entries.reason: Case report of exertional rhabdomyolysis after curls to failure (clinical/biochemical outcome); page otherwise references. Re-check 2026-10-02 (whole text, guidance/cause sentences): the only form mention is protocol - an elbow stabiliser kept full ROM and stopped elbow swing; no guidance. Full read 2026-10-02 (user request): no form fault is described; the only arm-position text is the protocol (back against the wall, elbow stabiliser for full ROM and no elbow swing). The discussion suggests the full ROM enforced by the stabiliser may have added muscle damage - read alone this argues against full ROM, the opposite of partial_curl feedback. The post-exercise inability to extend the arm is swelling from rhabdomyolysis, not a form fault.
